questions.question: Q1 For a 512-node 3D Torus, what is the worst-case hop count?
Q2 Why does Fat-Tree provide more predictable latency than 3D Torus?

answers.b: It has a fixed hop count regardless of cluster size

explanations.a: Incorrect. Cable speed is determined by the InfiniBand standard.
explanations.b: Correct. Fat-Tree guarantees H=4 for all node pairs, ensuring consistent latency.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Node count is independent of topology.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Fat-Tree uses multiple switch layers.

questions.question: Q3 Doubling the InfiniBand link speed from NDR to XDR affects serialization latency by:

explanations.c: Correct. Ts = S/Bandwidth; doubling bandwidth halves serialization time.

questions.question: Q4 In a 1024-node cluster, which topology has fewer worst-case hops?

explanations.a: Correct. Fat-Tree maintains 4 hops while 3D Torus has ⌊³√1024⌋ ≈ 10 hops.

questions.question: Q5 What is the serialization latency for a 100 MB payload on NDR (400 Gbps = 50 GB/s)?

explanations.b: Correct. Ts = 100 MB / 50 GB/s = 0.1/50 s = 2 ms.

questions.question: Q6 Why are Fat-Tree topologies preferred for AI training clusters despite higher cost?

answers.b: They provide consistent low latency at any scale

explanations.a: Incorrect. Fat-Trees are more complex to cable.
explanations.b: Correct. Predictable 4-hop latency ensures consistent performance for latency-sensitive AI workloads.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Power consumption depends on many factors.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Fat-Trees typically use more switches.

questions.question: Q7 What component of total delay is most affected by increasing cluster size in a 3D Torus?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Serialization depends on payload and bandwidth.
explanations.b: Correct. More nodes means more hops (H = ⌊³√N⌋), increasing switch processing delay.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Propagation delay depends on physical distance.

questions.question: Q8 What is the wrap-around connection in a 3D Torus?

answers.b: A connection linking opposite edges of the grid to form a closed loop

explanations.b: Correct. Wrap-around connections create the torus shape by linking opposite grid boundaries.

questions.question: Q9 Which delay component is independent of network topology?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Hop count varies by topology.
explanations.b: Correct. Serialization latency depends only on payload size and link bandwidth.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Total switch delay depends on hop count.

questions.question: Q10 What is the primary engineering trade-off demonstrated by this experiment?

answers.b: Latency predictability and performance vs cabling cost and complexity

explanations.b: Correct. Fat-Tree offers better performance at higher cost; 3D Torus is cheaper but has variable latency.
